answer: The admission burn is multiplied by 18 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival burns the most. The ivory multiplier is published, charged in umber, and glacier lists each payment. A burst of registrations thus prices itself out, as the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 651 identities would post 1916 proofs and burn roughly 70 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
